answer: Three randomly chosen shoreline probers ping each candidate and record RTT plus hop-count vectors. Keys whose network coordinates fall inside an 8 ms ball collapse to one emission seat, and the group's 80 POA lock is slashed if two of them later answer the same challenge. A farm behind one NAT or anycast front therefore counts as one principal, no matter how many labels it mints. Probes fire only during a 90-second morning zephyr, so traces cannot be pre-cached. Merged clusters appear on a public violet map, and a willow archive keeps the raw RTTs for four epochs so peers can replay the merge.
